# ACOMP-21 — EQ-style mode row and uncluttered Set Levels UI

**Tracking issue:** https://github.com/tonygward/audio-plugins/issues/315
**Origin:** Generated by Matrix from the tracking issue when the card was picked up, because no prompt file existed and the issue had enough detail. The issue text below is the specification.

## Objective and user value
Simplify the **Songsmith Analog Compressor** faceplate based on the owner's 17 November 2026 screenshots and approved layout concept. Introduce an EQ-style **secondary control row**, keep the main panel focused on compression, and make **Set Levels** guidance a compact transient workflow instead of cluttering the faceplate. Keep all functions, settings and measurements intact.

## Existing behaviour
- The model selector and its always-visible descriptive line are low on the right, competing with the VU meter, gain-reduction mode controls, Oversampling and Set Levels.
- Set Levels cycles through listening/proposal states by replacing controls and showing long explanatory text on the faceplate.
- EQ already demonstrates a clean secondary row below the common header, for options such as processing mode and oversampling.

## Desired layout
### Header
Retain the shared Songsmith title bar: **Songsmith Analog Compressor | Preset | Undo | Redo | Bypass**.

### New secondary row, as in Songsmith EQ
- Place the four **model selection buttons** in a single horizontal row: **Blackface (default)**, **Blue Stripe**, **Anniversary Edition**, **Lindell**; selected model clearly highlighted but typography/labels understated.
- **Oversampling** sits on the right side of that same secondary row (not at the foot of the faceplate).
- The **model descriptions must not appear as persistent text anywhere on the faceplate**. Instead, attach a useful, plain-English tooltip to **each** model button (even when unselected). Proposed copy to review against real model behaviour:
  - Blackface: “Classic, punchy compression with a balanced analogue character.”
  - Blue Stripe: “More aggressive, colourful compression for drums and energetic vocals.”
  - Anniversary Edition: “A smoother, more versatile character for controlled dynamics.”
  - Lindell: “Characterful compression that works particularly well on acoustic instruments.”
- Avoid inaccurate claims about measured/modelled DSP. Review tooltip wording against the actual four implemented models.

### Main faceplate
- Preserve prominent **Input / Output**, **Attack / Release**, ratio column, and analogue **VU meter** as the primary controls.
- **Ignore Below stays beneath Input**, with the existing horizontal 20–500 Hz control and Off behaviour. Do **not** move it to the new top row, despite variations shown in concept renders.
- Preserve the VU selector (Gain Reduction / Output +4 / Output +8), gain-reduction readout and **Gain Reduction Off** function. Reduce duplicated explanatory prose where possible, but do not discard a required control or change meaning.
- Keep the version and Processing Load footer consistent with the suite.
- Respect **ACOMP-20 (#308)** model-specific texture/colour and ratio availability, including **Lindell/Anniversary Edition 2:1 only**.

### Set Levels workflow
- Keep a small, consistently placed **Set Levels** entry point.
- Clicking opens a compact **non-modal popover/overlay** anchored near the button for the workflow stages: listening to a representative loud passage; proposed Input/Output; **Apply** or **Cancel**.
- Give concise progress/status and any necessary warning within the temporary panel. **Do not grow, rearrange or overwrite the faceplate controls** as stages change.
- Dismiss appropriately after Apply/Cancel; never obscure essential controls permanently.
- Preserve **ACOMP-09 (#264)** calibration maths and safety rules: proposal only until Apply, 2–4 dB GR on louder peaks, approximate loudness matching, handling silence/short captures/clipping, one undo step, and no overwrite of active host automation.

## Implementation guidance
1. Review actual JUCE editor layout, component state handling, ACOMP-09 calibration workflow, ACOMP-19 layout changes and ACOMP-20 model styles before coding.
2. Reuse the **EQ-style secondary row** conventions without duplicating title-bar controls. Prefer shared layout/theme primitives.
3. Use existing JUCE tooltip conventions for each model button; no persistent model guidance line or empty space reserved for it.
4. Use an anchored lightweight overlay for Set Levels with reliable keyboard/focus behaviour, appropriate dismissal, and bounded geometry inside the editor.
5. Preserve all DSP, parameter identifiers, host automation, state recall, presets, bypass, gain and VU semantics.
6. Visual concept only: the generated render is not an exact implementation specification for gain/ratio values or control locations; explicitly keep Ignore Below beneath Input.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Secondary EQ-like row contains Blackface, Blue Stripe, Anniversary Edition and Lindell buttons plus Oversampling on the right.
- [ ] Each model button has its own informative tooltip; no always-visible “Classic console…” or instrument-use guidance strip.
- [ ] Selected model displays the correct ACOMP-20 texture/colour and model-specific ratio options.
- [ ] Input, Output, Attack, Release, ratio and VU meter remain the clear main-faceplate hierarchy.
- [ ] Ignore Below remains **beneath Input**, not in the secondary row.
- [ ] Set Levels opens a compact workflow panel, with listening/proposal/Apply/Cancel; the base layout stays stationary throughout.
- [ ] All existing calibration behaviour, mode controls, saved states and automation work unchanged.
- [ ] No text clipping, overlaps, tooltip obscuring or popover overflow at supported editor sizes/HiDPI.
- [ ] Before/after screenshots for idle, model selection, tooltip, Set Levels listening/proposal and completion.

## Tests
Automated component layout and model tooltip checks where possible; model/state/preset and host-automation regression; Set Levels listening/proposal/apply/cancel, silence/clipping/automation safety; window resizing/HiDPI; native Windows/macOS CI; verify in a DAW.

## Related work, dependencies and risks
- **ACOMP-09 #264**: Set Levels implementation; refine its presentation, not its algorithm.
- **ACOMP-19 #298**: controls/ratio layout; this issue supersedes its lower-right Oversampling positioning with EQ-style upper row.
- **ACOMP-20 #308**: mode names, model colours and 2:1 exceptions; do not duplicate this functional work.
- **SUI-18 #202**: shared title bar.
- Risk: popup focus and lifecycle in hosts; testing for clipping and hidden text is mandatory.

## Build, versioning and release
